Investors made few changes to petroleum positions last week even as prices soared to four-month highs amid increasingly bellicose rhetoric from the United States and Iran about a possible resumption of fighting in the Gulf.

Hedge funds and other money managers purchased the equivalent of just 7 million barrels in the six most important futures and options contracts over the seven days ending on October 20, according to regulatory data ...

UPDATE: We now have new reason to believe that two of the three shipments are UAN fertilizer. The issue is that they departed from a petroleum berth in St. Petersburg, Russia and are heading to oil-centric terminals in USA even though one of the terminals hasn't imported Russian UAN in two years and the other shows no record of doing so. The third vessel is AGIOI FANENDES (9798375), which departed Primorsk's diesel terminal and was initialy stating "USNY" as her destination.

Prior to the war, the SoH handled 83% of crude oil exports from the Middle East. Today, it handles only 63% because the Red Sea has more than tripled its output. The SoH is losing relevance; and that is the goal for a long term, secured supply of energy.
